\section{Introduction}

A long read spans several heterozygous variants, so the reads of a diploid sample and its heterozygous variants can be phased together: each read is assigned to the parental haplotype it was sequenced from, and each variant allele to the haplotype whose reads carry it \citep{Patterson2015,Edge2017}. Phased variants give haplotypes; phased reads, tagged with their haplotype, are themselves the input of haplotype-resolved analyses, from allele-specific methylation and expression to the local assembly and structural variant calling of each haplotype. Long, accurate reads such as PacBio HiFi \citep{Wenger2019} make both possible from a single sample, without parental data.

Read-based phasers differ in how they solve the problem. WhatsHap minimises the number of read alleles that must be corrected for the reads to split into two haplotypes \citep{Patterson2015,Martin2016}, HapCUT2 maximises a likelihood by iterated cuts \citep{Edge2017}, LongPhase finds the two heaviest disjoint paths through a graph of variants linked by reads, and phases structural variants with them \citep{Lin2022}, and HiPhase searches with A* and phases small, structural and tandem repeat variants jointly \citep{Holt2024}. Each phases a set of variants a caller found on a linear reference, typically DeepVariant \citep{Poplin2018,Shafin2021}; longcallD calls and phases variants together, resolving noisy regions with local multiple sequence alignment \citep{Gao2026}.

Phasing through variants called on a linear reference has two weaknesses that affect reads more than variants. Where the caller finds no heterozygous variant, as in many tandem repeats and other regions where read alignments disagree, the reads there carry nothing to be phased by and stay unphased. Where a region is duplicated in the sample but not in the reference, the reads of both copies align to one place, and the copies' differences look like heterozygous variants. Such differences co-segregate with the reads as consistently as real heterozygous variants do, so a phaser can join two blocks through them in the wrong orientation and misphase every read beyond the join. Phasers are usually compared by their phased variants, through switch errors and block lengths \citep{Lin2022,Holt2024}. These metrics count a wrong join as one switch however many reads it misphases, and do not count the reads left unphased.

A pangenome graph represents the known alleles of many genomes at once \citep{Liao2023,Hickey2024}, and graph aligners place reads on it \citep{Garrison2018,Siren2021}. Where a read crosses a site of the graph, a snarl \citep{Paten2018}, the walk its alignment takes names the allele it carries, so the allele is observed without being called, including in repeats where alignments to a single reference place the same variant inconsistently. Pangenome references have been used to genotype known variants \citep{Siren2021,Ebler2022}. Known alleles alone cannot phase a sample, however, because every genome carries rare and private heterozygous variants that the graph does not contain.

pgphase phases reads with both kinds of variant. Our contributions are:

\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Phasing at known alleles from graph alignments} (Sections 2.2--2.3): a catalog of the sites of a pangenome graph, and each read's allele at them taken from its graph alignment.
  \item \textbf{One solve over the catalog's sites and the sample's own} (Sections 2.4--2.5): heterozygous variants found in the linear alignments, including those a multiple sequence alignment resolves in noisy regions, join the catalog's sites before phasing, and an expectation-maximization learns the error rate of every site, shrunk toward that of sites of the same kind.
  \item \textbf{Joins that the reads verify} (Section 2.6): two blocks are joined only when several reads carry evidence on both sides at reliable sites; sites at collapsed duplications, sites read only at low mapping quality and one-base length differences cannot join blocks, although they still label reads.
  \item \textbf{Read-level evaluation} (Section 2.8): the parent of origin of every read as truth, chromosomes not used for tuning, and each switch error classified by comparing the tool's haplotype sequences with the truth's.
\end{enumerate}

On each of eight chromosomes of HG002, including the three not used for tuning, pgphase phased more reads correctly, left fewer reads misphased or unphased, and made fewer switch errors than HiPhase, LongPhase, WhatsHap and longcallD (Table~\ref{tab:reads}; Table~\ref{tab:switches}).
